name: SlidesGPT
description: Use SlidesGPT to generate presentations with AI. First, name a topic that the presentation should be about. SlidesGPT will generate your presentation slides. Finally you can export to PowerPoint. Available features include: generate a structure and outline for a presentation, choose layouts and themes, refine slide content in a chat-based conversation, export and download as PowerPoint, Google Slides, PDF, and more.

tool.name: create_slides
tool.title: Create Slides
tool.description:
Create one or more professional presentation slides. Pass a single slide in the array for one slide, or multiple slides for a full deck.

WHEN TO USE — when the user has clearly asked for slides:
- User mentions any of: "slide", "presentation", "deck", "pitch deck", "pitchdeck", "pitch", "slideshow", "ppt", or "keynote"
- ANY intent phrasing about slides:
  • COMMANDS: "create", "make", "give me", "build", "generate", "design"
  • REQUESTS: "I need", "I want", "can you make", "could you create", "help me make"
  • SUGGESTIONS: "let's make", "let's create", "how about a presentation on"
  • IMPLIED: "deck about X", "pitch deck for X", "presentation on X" (even without a verb)
- If user asks for "a slide about X" (singular) and the topic warrants multiple slides, generate a single slide itself
- When user intent is ambiguous (e.g., "a deck about X" with no slide count), default to 2-3 slides

ATTACHED PDFs / DOCUMENTS: Claude ingests user-attached files as document content blocks directly in the conversation. Read the document content from the conversation and pass the relevant material (topic, structure, key points) into this tool's slides argument — there is no separate file upload step.

CRITICAL RULES:
- Pass all slides in a SINGLE call — NEVER call this tool multiple times in sequence
- When adding to an existing presentation, pass the presentation_id from the previous response IMPORTANT: DO NOT SKIP THIS STEP
- If no presentation_id exists, pass empty string — a new presentation will be created

THEMES: If the user asked for a specific theme, pass theme_id here — do NOT call apply_theme separately afterwards.

SLIDE FIELDS — EVERY slide MUST include all of these (the server does not fill them in for you):
- title: the slide title
- subtitle: one short phrase (4-10 words) that supports the title. Never empty.
- slidenum: 0-based position. A new deck starts at 0. When adding to an existing presentation, continue after its last slide.
- layout: one of the LAYOUT OPTIONS below
- body: 3-5 items (see CONTENT REQUIREMENTS). A "title_and_subtitle" slide may have fewer.
- talktrack: speaker notes, 2-3 sentences the presenter says aloud. Expand on the bullets instead of repeating them.
- image_caption: the ideal slide image in 8-10 words (subject, setting, mood). Leave image_id empty; the system uses your caption to find the best matching photo.

LAYOUT VARIETY RULES (CRITICAL for multi-slide decks):
1. Use a VARIETY of layouts across the deck. Match each layout to the slide's content.
2. Slide 0 of a NEW deck is the title slide: use "title_and_subtitle".
3. The FIRST content slide SHOULD use "title_and_two_columns" (image layout).
4. Decks of 5+ slides MUST use at least 4 different layouts.
5. NEVER repeat the same layout for consecutive slides.
6. Use "title_and_two_to_four_columns_with_icons" for AT MOST 2 slides per deck.
7. Use "title_and_body" for AT MOST 1 slide (conclusion only).
8. Use metric_rings ONLY for percentage-based metrics (0-100).
9. Mix visual variety: combine image slides, charts, timelines, grids, and text slides.

LAYOUT OPTIONS (set layout for EVERY slide):
- "title_and_two_columns": Content with image alongside bullets (IMAGE LAYOUT)
- "title_and_two_to_four_columns_with_icons": 2-4 key points with icons
- "title_and_body": Single-column bullets (use sparingly — AT MOST 1 per deck, conclusion only)
- "title_and_subtitle": Section divider or transition slide (title + subtitle only, minimal body)
- "image_full_width": Full-width image with optional text below (IMAGE LAYOUT)
- "image_left_text_right": Image on the left with bullet points on the right (IMAGE LAYOUT)
- "quadrant_grid": EXACTLY 4 comparable items — SWOT, 2x2 matrices, pros/cons
- "data_table": Structured tabular data. REQUIRES the "table" field with a markdown table (header + separator + rows)
- "chart_bar": Numeric comparisons across categories (e.g., revenue by region, sales by product). REQUIRES the "chart" field with type "bar"
- "chart_pie": Part-of-whole composition (market share, budget split, % breakdown). REQUIRES the "chart" field with type "pie"
- "timeline_horizontal": Chronological events, milestones, or history (dates in point, short descriptions)
- "layered_pyramid": Hierarchical structures with 3-6 levels (MUST include icon with fa- prefix per item)
- "phase_roadmap": Project phases with milestones — point MUST use "Period: Title" format (e.g., "Q1 2024: Launch")
- "metric_rings": KPIs, completion rates, market share (1-4 metrics, values 0-100 as percentages)

CONTENT REQUIREMENTS:
- 3-5 substantial bullet points per slide
- Each bullet description: 2-4 lines with specific data, evidence, or actionable insights
- Content should be PhD-level, detailed, and evidence-driven
- Use FontAwesome 5.15 icons (e.g., fa-bolt, fa-chart-line, fa-lightbulb)
- EVERY body item MUST include "value" (0-100) — enables chart rendering and layout switching
- For chart_bar / chart_pie / data_table slides: ALSO emit a body[] array (3-5 items summarising the chart/table) so the slide still has useful bullets if the user switches the layout

LAYOUT-SPECIFIC FORMATTING (MUST FOLLOW):
- quadrant_grid: EXACTLY 4 items. "point" under 15 chars, "description" under 80 chars
- timeline_horizontal: Dates/years in "point" (max 15 chars). "description" max 50 chars
- layered_pyramid: "icon" with fa- prefix REQUIRED (fa-star, fa-check, fa-rocket). 3-6 items
- phase_roadmap: "point" = "Period: Title" (e.g., "Q1 2024: Launch"). Max 4 phases. "description" = milestones separated by "; "
- metric_rings: 1-4 items. For part-of-whole metrics (market share), values sum to ~100. For standalone KPIs (NPS, satisfaction), each value stands alone
- data_table: emit "table": { "md": "| Header1 | Header2 |\n| --- | --- |\n| Row1Col1 | Row1Col2 |" }. Markdown table must have header, separator row of dashes, and at least one data row. Set the "chart" field to null on this slide.
- chart_bar: emit "chart": { "type": "bar", "title": "Revenue by Region", "unit": "$M", "data": [{ "label": "EMEA", "value": 4.2 }, { "label": "APAC", "value": 3.1 }] }. For multi-series (grouped/stacked bars), give every data point a "series" string and reuse the same labels across series. Optional: xTitle, yTitle, stacked. Set "table" to null.
- chart_pie: emit "chart": { "type": "pie", "title": "Market Share", "unit": "%", "data": [{ "label": "SegmentA", "value": 42 }, { "label": "SegmentB", "value": 31 }] }. Values should sum to ~100. Set "table" to null.

SCHEMA NOTE: For non-chart/non-table slides, set "chart" and "table" to null (or omit them).

EXAMPLE SLIDE (format only — write real content for the user's topic):
{ "title": "Why Remote Teams Win", "subtitle": "Productivity data from 2,000 companies", "slidenum": 1, "layout": "title_and_two_columns", "image_caption": "diverse team on video call in bright home office", "talktrack": "Remote teams now outperform office teams on output per hour. The gap is widest in engineering, where focus time matters most. Hiring reach is the second big win.", "body": [{ "point": "13% more output", "description": "Stanford study of 16,000 workers found remote staff completed more calls per shift with fewer sick days.", "icon": "fa-chart-line", "value": 13 }, { "point": "Wider talent pool", "description": "Companies hiring remotely fill senior roles 30% faster by recruiting beyond commuting distance.", "icon": "fa-globe", "value": 30 }, { "point": "Lower office costs", "description": "Average savings of $11,000 per employee per year on real estate, utilities and supplies.", "icon": "fa-piggy-bank", "value": 45 }], "chart": null, "table": null }

icon.description: FontAwesome 5.15 icon name (e.g., 'lightbulb', 'chart-line', 'rocket'). REQUIRED for layered_pyramid (use fa- prefix: 'fa-star', 'fa-check').

point.description: Main point (2-6 words). For timeline_horizontal: use dates/years (max 15 chars). For phase_roadmap: MUST use 'Period: Title' format (e.g., 'Q1 2024: Launch'). For quadrant_grid: keep under 15 chars.

value.description: REQUIRED for ALL layouts. Numeric value 0-100. For metric_rings: used directly for chart rendering (must be realistic percentages). For other layouts: preserved so users can switch layouts without losing data. For part-of-whole data (market share), values should sum to ~100.

description.description: Detailed explanation (2-4 lines). For timeline_horizontal: keep SHORT (max 50 chars). For quadrant_grid: max 80 chars. For phase_roadmap: milestones separated by '; '. For data_table: use key:value pairs. Otherwise include data, evidence, or insights.

body.description: Array of 3-5 substantial bullet points. EVERY item MUST include value (0-100). Follow layout-specific formatting rules from the tool description.

chart.description: REQUIRED for chart_bar and chart_pie layouts; null for every other layout. Shape: { type: "bar"|"pie", title?: string|null, unit?: string|null, data: [{ label: string, value: number, series?: string|null }] }. For chart_pie, values should sum to ~100 (or be plain percentages). For chart_bar, omit `series` for a single-series chart, or use it to group bars into a grouped/stacked chart. Bar-only optional fields: xTitle, yTitle, stacked (boolean).

table.description:
REQUIRED for data_table layout; null for every other layout. Shape: { md: "<markdown table>" }. The string MUST be a valid markdown table — header row, separator row of dashes, and at least one data row, all pipe-delimited. Example: "| Region | Revenue |
| --- | --- |
| EMEA | $4.2M |
| APAC | $3.1M |".

_published_faq.name: How do I add SlidesGPT to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add SlidesGPT to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://claude.slidesgpt.com/mcp.

_published_faq.name: Is SlidesGPT MCP ready for ChatGPT and Claude?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 6, 2026, SlidesGPT scores 88/100 on Manufact's MCP publishing checklist. The scan does not yet meet ChatGPT publishing checks and meets Claude publishing checks. Passing these checks does not guarantee marketplace approval.

_published_faq.name: How clear is SlidesGPT's MCP tool documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 6, 2026, SlidesGPT scores 77/100 in Manufact's review of tool titles, descriptions, input and output schemas, and behavior annotations. The review covers 2 of 2 discovered tools. The quality score measures documentation clarity; runtime behavior and marketplace readiness require separate checks.

_published_faq.name: What tools does the SlidesGPT MCP server provide?

acceptedAnswer.text: SlidesGPT provides these MCP tools: create_slides and apply_theme.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to SlidesGPT?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to SlidesGPT in design-creative on the Manufact MCP catalog include Motion, MotionVid, Sleek, Streamloop MCP, and Image Generation.
SlidesGPT does not require authentication. It is a public MCP endpoint you can connect without logging in.

_published_faq.name: How can SlidesGPT improve its MCP documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: create_slides is the lowest-scoring reviewed tool at 72/100. No output schema is declared. Add one for structured results so clients can interpret returned fields. Open its review for feedback and a copyable fix prompt, then rerun the documentation review after updating your tool metadata.
SlidesGPT is developed by Lightstone GmbH. It is listed as partner on the Claude connector directory.
